findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:12 — `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is off by one when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50 or 100 members with limit 50 → 2 or 3 pages reported instead of 1 or 2). Since `showingLast` compares `currentPage == totalPages`, "next" stays enabled and the admin lands on a phantom empty page. Should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:23 — `create` never assigns `alias_level` even though the client sends it (`Discourse.Group.asJSON()` includes `alias_level` in the POST), so newly created groups silently lose the admin-selected alias level (falling back to 0) until a separate manual re-save.

[Medium/api] app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Breaking change to the public `/groups/:name/members` response: it was a bare JSON array of all members and is now `{members: [...], meta: {...}}` silently truncated to 50 by default, so existing API consumers will either break on the shape change or silently receive partial member lists.

[Medium/test_gap] spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb — No specs added or updated for the public `groups#members` endpoint despite its response shape and pagination semantics being completely changed (limit/offset handling, meta block, count query).

[Low/api] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:33 — `update`/`create` no longer accept the nested `group[...]` parameter format (and the PATCH incremental `changes` API is removed) with no deprecation; a legacy payload like `group: {visible: "true"}` makes `params[:visible]` nil, so `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` silently flips `visible` to false for old-format clients.

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:15 — `findMembers` does a bare `return;` (undefined) when name is empty instead of returning a promise (`Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` as before), breaking any caller that chains `.then()` on the result (including `next`/`previous` actions that `return group.findMembers()`).

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — Pagination state is not reconciled after membership changes: `findMembers` clamps `offset` against the stale pre-fetch `user_count` and the server echoes back the requested offset in `meta.offset`, so removing the last member on the last page (e.g., 51 users, offset 50) leaves the admin on an empty page even though remaining members exist on the previous page.

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:4 — `usernames` is a plain property on a singleton controller and is never reset: usernames typed while editing one group persist in the input when switching to another group (risking adding users to the wrong group via `addMembers`), and it is not cleared after a successful add, so repeated clicks re-submit the same names.

[Low/bug] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:53 — `add_members` calls `usernames.split(",")` on the raw `params.require(:usernames)` value; if a client submits `usernames[]` (array), this raises `NoMethodError` and returns a 500 instead of a 422/400.

[Low/performance] app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — No upper-bound validation on `limit` for the public members endpoint; `?limit=1000000` serializes a group's entire membership in one response (memory/DoS exposure). `limit` should be clamped to a max.

[Low/concurrency] app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:33 — `next`/`previous` fire overlapping `findMembers()` requests with no cancellation/serialization; a slower stale response can resolve after the latest one and overwrite `offset`/`members` via `setProperties`, leaving the UI on a page inconsistent with the admin's clicks.

[Low/test_gap] spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:96 — the "cannot remove members from automatic groups" test invokes `xhr :put, :remove_member` although the route is DELETE; controller specs bypass routing, so the actual DELETE verb/route wiring for `remove_member` is never exercised and would pass even if the route were broken.

The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:23 — `create` never assigns `alias_level` even though the client sends it (`Discourse.Group.asJSON()` includes `alias_level` in the POST), so newly created groups silently lose the admin-selected alias level (falling back to 0) until a separate manual re-save.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: client POST for group creation uses `Discourse.Group.create()` which sends `data: this.asJSON()`, and `asJSON()` now includes `alias_level` (and `visible`, `name`). However `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` and `group.visible` and never assigns `group.alias_level` from `params[:alias_level]`, unlike `update` which does. This means newly created groups will ignore the admin-selected alias level and default to whatever the model default is (likely 0) until later update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Breaking change to the public `/groups/:name/members` response: it was a bare JSON array of all members and is now `{members: [...], meta: {...}}` silently truncated to 50 by default, so existing API consumers will either break on the shape change or silently receive partial member lists.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare array of members) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and introduces pagination with a default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` for all groups. This is a backwards-incompatible API response-shape change and also changes default behavior from “all members” (for non-automatic groups) to “first 50 unless limit/offset provided”, which can break existing consumers or silently return partial results. It may be intentional, but it’s a real compatibility concern grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb — No specs added or updated for the public `groups#members` endpoint despite its response shape and pagination semantics being completely changed (limit/offset handling, meta block, count query).

adjudication.rationale: The diff materially changes the public `GroupsController#members` endpoint from `render_serialized(members, GroupUserSerializer)` to a new JSON shape `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and changes pagination semantics to always apply `limit`/`offset` (plus a `count` query) regardless of `automatic?` (see `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`). However, the only specs modified are for `Admin::GroupsController` (`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`); there are no added/updated specs for `GroupsController#members` in this diff, so the stated test gap is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:33 — `update`/`create` no longer accept the nested `group[...]` parameter format (and the PATCH incremental `changes` API is removed) with no deprecation; a legacy payload like `group: {visible: "true"}` makes `params[:visible]` nil, so `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` silently flips `visible` to false for old-format clients.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Admin::GroupsController#create` and `#update` to read top-level params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:alias_level]`) instead of the previous nested `params[:group][...]` payload (and removes the old PATCH `changes` flow entirely). In the new `update`, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` will evaluate to `false` when `params[:visible]` is missing (e.g., an old client still sending `group: { visible: "true" }`), silently flipping `visible` to false. This behavior is directly implied by the new controller code in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — Pagination state is not reconciled after membership changes: `findMembers` clamps `offset` against the stale pre-fetch `user_count` and the server echoes back the requested offset in `meta.offset`, so removing the last member on the last page (e.g., 51 users, offset 50) leaves the admin on an empty page even though remaining members exist on the previous page.

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.findMembers` the requested `offset` is clamped using the *current client-side* `user_count` (`var self = this, offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));`). After `removeMember` / `addMembers`, the client calls `self.findMembers()` but `user_count` is stale until the response arrives. If you remove the only user on the last page (e.g. `user_count` was 51, `offset` 50, `limit` 50), the request still goes out with `offset=50`. Server-side `GroupsController#members` returns `total` after deletion (50) but uses the requested `offset` (50) and returns an empty `members` array with `meta.offset: 50`, and the model then sets `offset` to 50 and `members` to empty. Nothing in the diff reconciles `offset` against the new `meta.total`, so the UI can remain on an empty page even though previous-page members exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:4 — `usernames` is a plain property on a singleton controller and is never reset: usernames typed while editing one group persist in the input when switching to another group (risking adding users to the wrong group via `addMembers`), and it is not cleared after a successful add, so repeated clicks re-submit the same names.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `usernames` was changed from a computed property to a plain controller property (`usernames: null`) and is now bound to the add-members `user-selector` in `group.hbs` (`{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`). The route `setupController` now only sets `model` and calls `model.findMembers()` but does not reset `controller.usernames`, so any previously typed value can persist when navigating between groups using the same controller instance. Additionally, `actions.addMembers` explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not clear `this.get("usernames")` after calling `model.addMembers(...)`, so repeated clicks can resubmit the same usernames.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:53 — `add_members` calls `usernames.split(",")` on the raw `params.require(:usernames)` value; if a client submits `usernames[]` (array), this raises `NoMethodError` and returns a 500 instead of a 422/400.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff shows `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",")`. In Rails, a request can legally supply `usernames[]` params, making `params[:usernames]` an Array; `Array#split` does not exist, so this would raise `NoMethodError` and lead to a 500 (no rescue/validation is shown), rather than a controlled 4xx response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — No upper-bound validation on `limit` for the public members endpoint; `?limit=1000000` serializes a group's entire membership in one response (memory/DoS exposure). `limit` should be clamped to a max.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then applies it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit)` with no max clamp. This makes the public endpoint accept arbitrarily large `?limit=` values and serialize huge membership lists (plus `total = group.users.count`), creating a clear memory/DoS exposure grounded in the shown code.
